source_title: Canvix — Free & open-source graphic design tool. A community-built Canva alternative with a drag-and-drop editor, templates, shapes, text, images & one-click export. Works on desktop, tablet & mobile. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
Free & open-source graphic design tool — a community-built Canva alternative.
Features · Quick start · Self-hosting · Roadmap · Contributing
Canvix is a browser-based design tool that lets anyone create social media posts, presentations, posters, logos and thumbnails — with a drag-and-drop editor, a 110-template library and one-click export. It runs entirely on your own infrastructure, stores designs in your own database, and exports files locally in your browser. Free accounts keep your designs yours; anonymous link-editing keeps working too. No watermarks, no paywalls.
Every feature in Canvix is free, and it stays free. Forever. There is no Pro tier, no subscription, no trial countdown, no watermark ransom, no "premium" element you can drag but not drop. The whole point of this project is a design tool that never asks you for a credit card:
All 110 templates — including the entire premium collection — are free
All exports (PNG, JPG, SVG, PDF, video) are free and unwatermarked
All AI features (magic edit, magic write, background removal, translate) run against your own API keys, so there is nothing for us to meter
Accounts are free — username + password, no email, no verification, no external provider; a self-hoster runs the whole thing for $0
Self-hosting is first-class: your server, your database, your rules
The license is MIT — you can even fork it and build a business on it
If anyone ever asks you to pay for Canvix, you are being scammed: the source is right here.
v0.9.0 — Accounts & per-design ownership
Free accounts, zero dependencies — username + password with scrypt hashing from node:crypto and opaque DB-backed sessions (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookies; the DB stores only sha256(token) so a leak never yields usable sessions). No email, no OAuth, no external provider — deliberately self-contained so self-hosting stays free forever.
Per-design ownership — designs you create while signed in are private to your account: the dashboard scopes to “yours + shared”, and every mutating API (save, delete, restore, version snapshot) answers 403 for anyone else. Share links still open — in view-only mode with an honest banner in the editor.
Nothing breaks for existing setups — ownerless designs keep the exact pre-v0.9 link-editable behaviour. One click ( “Save my designs to this account” ) migrates the designs this browser created into your new account — anonymous creations are attributed to the creating browser ( canvix_anon cookie, sha256-hashed in the DB), so adopt-all can never sweep up another person's work . Legacy designs from before attribution exist? Claim those one-by-one with the per-design “Save to my account” action (a deliberate, visible action for pre-accounts self-hosters).
CSRF-safe writes — every mutating API route enforces same-origin on top of the SameSite=Lax session cookie; cross-site POST/PUT/DELETE requests answer 403 CSRF_REJECTED . Non-browser clients (curl, the MCP endpoint) are unaffected.
Collab identity upgrade — signed-in users appear under their real username in presence, cursors and comments.
DNS-rebinding pinning (SSRF close-out) — the MCP server's safeFetch now connects via a custom lookup pinned to the validated IP, closing the TOCTOU window documented in v0.6.1. TLS keeps the real hostname for SNI, so certificate validation is unaffected.
End-to-end CI verification — the “Canvix Database Setup” workflow now boots the built server against your real database and exercises the whole account + ownership + claim-safety + CSRF flow (register → me → owned create → owner save → anonymous 403 → logout → revoked-token replay → login → cross-origin rejection → two-browser adopt-all scoping → cross-account isolation) before cleaning up after itself.
v0.8.0 — Supabase-ready infrastructure & the 110-template library
Supabase-first database support — switching hosts (Neon → Supabase, or anything else) is now a two-command move: Real migrations — prisma/migrations ships in the repo, so npm run db:setup creates the full schema on a brand-new database (Supabase, Neon, RDS, local…) and seeds the template library in one go Self-healing setup — if your database was provisioned with the pre-v0.8 db push flow, db:setup detects it, baselines the migration history (Prisma's documented path) and continues instead of dead-ending Smart connection handling ( src/lib/db-url.ts ) — a copy-pasted Supabase connection string just works: TLS is auto-required for remote hosts, and the transaction pooler (port 6543) automatically gets pgbouncer-compatible settings so prepared statements don't break /api/health — a one-page diagnosis of env → connectivity → migration → seed, with the exact fix printed at each step Actionable errors everywhere — “Could not open template” is dead: API failures now carry classified codes ( DB_NOT_MIGRATED , DB_UNREACHABLE …), the dashboard shows a setup banner with the fix, and toasts tell you exactly what to run

Self-healing setup — if your database was provisioned with the pre-v0.8 db push flow, db:setup detects it, baselines the migration history (Prisma's documented path) and continues instead of dead-ending
Smart connection handling ( src/lib/db-url.ts ) — a copy-pasted Supabase connection string just works: TLS is auto-required for remote hosts, and the transaction pooler (port 6543) automatically gets pgbouncer-compatible settings so prepared statements don't break
/api/health — a one-page diagnosis of env → connectivity → migration → seed, with the exact fix printed at each step
Actionable errors everywhere — “Could not open template” is dead: API failures now carry classified codes ( DB_NOT_MIGRATED , DB_UNREACHABLE …), the dashboard shows a setup banner with the fix, and toasts tell you exactly what to run
The template library, ×1.8 — now 110 templates, all free — 50 new 2026-trend originals across every category, authored in-house (podcast quote card, new-listing post, bootcamp, restaurant special, lookbook, webinar, LinkedIn banner, recipe pin, birthday story, Black Friday, playlist cover, flash-sale countdown, grand opening · investor pitch, marketing plan, course, agency portfolio, quarterly review, demo day, nonprofit impact, product launch · wedding invitation, gym flyer, cafe menu, concert poster, yoga flyer, gift certificate, business card, open mic, moving sale · executive & creative resumes, cover letter, proposal, invoice, newsletter, whitepaper, agenda, press release · 7 thumbnails · 3 logos). The library lives in src/lib/templates/ as collections so it can keep growing, and a validator ( scripts/validate-templates.ts ) checks every entry at CI time
v0.7.0 — Fast & Free Forever: rendering performance & the premium template collection
Rendering performance — the canvas was rebuilt around three classic hot-path killers, and every one is gone: Structural sharing in the editor store — every mutation now builds only the pages/elements it actually touches; untouched objects keep their identity. A keystroke, a slider drag or a remote/AI live edit re-renders exactly one canvas node instead of the whole scene, and deep-cloning the entire document per edit is history O(1) undo/redo — history snapshots now share structure with live state (like Immer, without Immer): pushing history is a reference copy, and a 60-step history of a large design costs a fraction of the old memory Memoized canvas nodes — ElementNode no longer subscribes to the whole store (it reads actions at event time via getState() ), is wrapped in React.memo , and receives stable callbacks — so selection changes, panel toggles and remote cursors don't re-render a single shape Split Konva layers — interaction chrome (transformer, snap guides, marquee, ruler guides, draw preview) moved to its own layer: dragging an element no longer repaints the chrome, and guide updates no longer repaint the artwork Snap-guide equality guard — identical guide sets don't trigger a React render; snapping during drag only redraws when something visibly changed Shared image cache — images decode once per URL and are reused across pages, thumbnails and duplicated nodes (with in-flight dedup and a bounded 300-entry LRU) perfectDrawEnabled: false on element nodes — skips Konva's hit-canvas perfection pass during drag/transform for a big interactive win Lazy template thumbnails — preview stages mount via IntersectionObserver (300 px pre-roll), so scrolling the 110-template library stays smooth; only visible cards own a canvas Locked in by tests: src/store/editor-store.test.ts asserts the identity guarantees (untouched pages/elements keep references, history shares structure, snapshots are never mutated in place)

A keystroke, a slider drag or a remote/AI live edit re-renders exactly one canvas node instead of the whole scene, and deep-cloning the entire document per edit is history
O(1) undo/redo — history snapshots now share structure with live state (like Immer, without Immer): pushing history is a reference copy, and a 60-step history of a large design costs a fraction of the old memory
Memoized canvas nodes — ElementNode no longer subscribes to the whole store (it reads actions at event time via getState() ), is wrapped in React.memo , and receives stable callbacks — so selection changes, panel toggles and remote cursors don't re-render a single shape
Split Konva layers — interaction chrome (transformer, snap guides, marquee, ruler guides, draw preview) moved to its own layer: dragging an element no longer repaints the chrome, and guide updates no longer repaint the artwork
Snap-guide equality guard — identical guide sets don't trigger a React render; snapping during drag only redraws when something visibly changed
Shared image cache — images decode once per URL and are reused across pages, thumbnails and duplicated nodes (with in-flight dedup and a bounded 300-entry LRU)
perfectDrawEnabled: false on element nodes — skips Konva's hit-canvas perfection pass during drag/transform for a big interactive win
Lazy template thumbnails — preview stages mount via IntersectionObserver (300 px pre-roll), so scrolling the 110-template library stays smooth; only visible cards own a canvas
Locked in by tests: src/store/editor-store.test.ts asserts the identity guarantees (untouched pages/elements keep references, history shares structure, snapshots are never mutated in place)
The premium template collection — all free — 39 new templates (21 → 60), every one designed to Canva-grade quality and every one unlocked: social (flash sale story, trattoria, open house, bootcamp, webinar, podcast cover, birthday story, wanderlust, LinkedIn banner, minimal quote), presentations (pitch deck noir, quarterly report, webinar deck, course welcome, roadmap, meet-the-team), print (neon gig poster, charity gala, artisan menu, spa voucher, yard sign, luxe card, wedding thank-you, coupon), documents (proposal, newsletter, ebook cover, whitepaper, press release, meeting agenda, studio invoice, case study), thumbnails (gaming, tutorial, podcast episode, unboxing) and logos (orbit, bloom, apex). The templates panel gets a "Premium collection · free forever" section — premium is a quality label here, never a paywall
v0.6.0 — the Agent Edition: MCP, tables, frames, curved text & embeds
MCP server (Model Context Protocol) — Canvix becomes an agent-native design platform : POST /api/mcp speaks standard MCP (JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP, stateless — same transport profile Canva's AI Connector uses), so AI assistants like Claude Desktop, Cursor, ChatGPT and any MCP client can create and edit real designs on your server . 20 tools : browse templates, search/get/create designs, add text/shapes/images/tables/embeds, restyle & move elements, set backgrounds, animate pages, comment, and export (SVG/PNG/JSON) — plus generate_design , which asks the server AI provider for a structured, fully-validated page layout and materializes it as native editable elements. Every tool maps to a real subsystem; without a provider everything works except generate_design , which says so plainly. Agent edits append to the same event log the editor replays, so a design an agent is editing updates live for humans in the editor
Security by default — the endpoint stays disabled until you set CANVIX_MCP_TOKEN ; requests need Authorization: Bearer (timing-safe compare), cross-origin requests are rejected, per-IP rate limits apply, image fetches are SSRF-guarded (private hosts denied, 8 MB cap), patches are whitelisted & clamped per element type, and errors never leak stack traces
Tables — Canva-style native tables: click any cell on the canvas to edit it, add/remove rows & columns from the toolbar, style borders/header/text, four starter styles. Cells export to SVG and translate with the design
Frames — image-in-shape frames (rectangle, rounded, ellipse, circle, triangle, hexagon). Drop an upload or photo on a frame to fill it — the image is clipped to the shape with cover-fit (also true vector in SVG export)
Curved text — Canva's signature arc effect: curve any text −180°…+180° (arch up / valley down), rendered as a real text-on-path (Konva TextPath , SVG ) so it stays crisp in PNG/PDF/video exports and editable everywhere
Embed cards — YouTube videos, Google Maps places and any link become native vector link cards (media band, play/pin glyph, title). Clicking a card in Preview or shared views opens the URL — honest scope: a styled card, not an iframe
Translate covers tables — the AI translator now also walks table cells, not just text boxes
Dashboard “AI agents (MCP)” card — shows the live endpoint status and a copy-paste client config (endpoint URL + bearer headers) for Claude Desktop / Cursor / any MCP client
v0.5.0 — Magic Layers, real-time collaboration & production AI infrastructure
Magic Layers — upload any flat design (or pick an image on your canvas) and a vision model decomposes it into real, editable Canvix layers : text becomes live text boxes (color, weight and size recovered), photos become cropped image elements, shapes become native shapes, the background becomes a page background. Every region carries a confidence score — uncertain regions are flagged amber in the review step and can be discarded. Honest limitations are surfaced in-product (fonts are matched by class, not recovered exactly; illustrations become image regions)
Real-time collaboration — share a design link and edit together: live multiplayer with colored cursors + name tags , remote selection outlines, presence avatars in the top bar, a live/offline connection indicator, and gap-free catch-up after disconnects. Architecture: an append-only event log in Postgres + server-sent events downstream + batched op POSTs upstream — works on Vercel serverless and self-hosted Node alike, no WebSocket server required. Link access (documented in the Share dialog since v0.11.7): anyone who can reach your instance can open a share link; ownerless designs (created while signed out) are editable by everyone with the link, while designs owned by an account open read-only for everyone else — there is no cloud gatekeeping, reachability is decided by your deployment. Optimistic local edits always keep the canvas butter-smooth. Since v0.10 collaboration is also offline-safe : edits made while disconnected (or after a crash/reload) queue in IndexedDB and merge deterministically on reconnect — every element is a hybrid-logical-clock-stamped last-write-wins register with delete tombstones, and the server merges divergent autosaves with the same pure rule every client runs, so no one's work is ever silently overwritten (see research/OFFLINE-MERGE.md )
Comments & annotations — a first-class comments mode: click anywhere on the canvas (or on an element — the pin follows it) to drop a threaded comment. Replies, resolve/reopen, delete-own, unread badges, collaborator avatars and live propagation to everyone in the design
Animations — Magic Animate — an Animate panel (Page / Element tabs) with 9 element animations (fade, rise, pan, pop, wipe, zoom, rotate, breathe), speed presets, duration/delay/easing/direction controls, and page transitions (fade/slide/morph, 0.1–2.5 s). One-click Magic Animate gives the whole page a tasteful animation pass. Animated playback in Preview with autoplay and a reduce-motion accessibility toggle
SVG export — true vector export: text, shapes, paths, gradients, opacity, transforms, images and shadows serialize to clean, sanitized SVG (no rasterization of vector elements, opens in browsers and vector editors)
Video export (MP4/WebM) — a real rendering pipeline: the animation timeline is rendered frame-by-frame to an offscreen canvas and encoded locally via MediaRecorder — MP4 (H.264) where the browser can encode it, WebM otherwise. Honest format detection is shown before you export. No uploads, no server rendering. Since v0.11 the page's audio is muxed into the recording (best-effort per browser) and beat-synced pulses render into the video
Audio/video elements & Beat Sync (v0.11) — upload MP3/WAV/MP4/WebM through the chunked media store (works within every serverless body limit); audio renders as a waveform card with the tempo detected in-browser, video as a poster frame. Media plays in Preview/Present, and any element can pulse on the music's beats — in the editor preview, presentation and exported video. See research/MEDIA-AND-BEAT-SYNC.md
AI Assistant 2.0 — the assistant is now design-aware: it sees your page's elements, colors, fonts and selection, and answers with structured, validated actions ("move the title to the top", "change all heading colors to purple", "make the layout more balanced", "add a CTA"). Every change lands as a normal, undoable edit
AI provider abstraction — all AI features route through one server-side provider layer: per-IP rate limits, usage accounting, capability probing and graceful degradation when no provider is configured (local features like background removal, palette generation and layout balancing keep working; the rest show a clear "requires an AI provider" notice)
v0.4.0 — the Magic Suite: AI editing, PostgreSQL & infrastructure
PostgreSQL database — Prisma migrated from SQLite to Postgres (native jsonb documents); one database technology everywhere, local & serverless-ready (Neon / Supabase / RDS). Includes the .env.example Postgres URL guide
Magic Resize — Canva Magic-Switch-style resize dialog: check any of 12 channel presets (Story / Reels / posts / A4 / poster / business card…), then resize in place or Copy & resize — every copy gets an automatic smart re-layout (elements scale, keep their relative positions, fonts & strokes re-proportion)
BG Remover — one-click background removal on any selected image, powered by an in-browser ONNX segmentation model (real alpha cut-outs, first use downloads the model once, then it's cached)
Magic Eraser — describe an unwanted object ("the person in the background") and AI removes it, reconstructing the background behind it
Enhance image — one-click AI photo cleanup: sharpening, lighting and colour balance while keeping the framing identical
Translate design — File → Translate: pick from 24 languages, and every text across all pages is AI-translated in place (layout intact, one undo)
Canvix AI assistant — a chat copilot app (Canva AI-style) that sees your design: ask for headlines, palettes or taglines and tap the suggested actions to add text, generate images, save palettes or translate the design
Live photo search — the Photos panel now searches real web photos (not just the bundled library) with debounced live results
Server-side version history — snapshots now persist in Postgres (30 per design, cascade-deleted), with localStorage as an offline fallback
Dashboard trash — deleting a design moves it to a Trash section (restore / delete forever), plus a Recent/Name sort control
5 new document templates — Minimal Resume, Certificate of Achievement, Clean Invoice, Monthly Calendar and Business Card under a new "Docs & office" category (21 templates total)
v0.3.2 — fonts, gradients, PDF, photos & AI
63-font library — 15 → 63 families across five categories (sans / serif / display / handwriting / new Mono ) in a searchable, pill-filtered Canva-style font dropdown
Gradient fills — linear & radial gradients on all shapes and text , edited straight in the colour menu: preset swatches, Linear/Radial toggle, 0-360° angle slider, from/to colour pickers, one-click remove
PDF export — print-ready, multi-page PDF downloads straight from the browser (jsPDF, zero watermarks)
Photos tab — new side panel with a bundled, license-free stock library (7 categories × 6 AI-generated photos), tag search, category chips and click-to-place
Magic Write — AI copywriter app: describe what you need, pick kind (headline / tagline / body / caption) and tone, get 3 on-brand options, add one to the canvas
AI image generator — prompt + style + aspect ratio → a design-ready image on your canvas
Design Trends 2026 templates — five templates from Canva's official 2026 trend report: Prompt Playground, Notes App Chic, Texture Check, Opt Out Era and Granny Wave
Per-page guides — ruler guides now belong to their page; snapping and Clear-guides act on the current page only
v0.3.1 — editor completeness: rulers, crop, layers rename, version history
Rulers & manual guides — Canva-style ruler strips (top/left) with adaptive tick ladders and pointer markers; drag out of a ruler to pull a #9954FF guide, drag it to move, drag off-page or double-click to delete, and snap elements to it. Toggle with Shift+R or the File menu
Image crop — select an image → Crop button (or right-click → Crop image): drag handles or draw a brand-new crop region, lock to aspect presets (1:1, 4:3, 16:9…), rule-of-thirds overlay, live pixel readout, flips baked in
Layer renaming — double-click any row in the Layers list for an inline rename; custom names persist with the design
Version history — File → Version history (or Ctrl+Alt+S ): labelled local snapshots per design with restore (undo-able), delete and relative timestamps
Group rotation fixed & refined — rotating a group no longer double-rotates its children, and ungrouping a rotated group keeps every child exactly where it was
Clickable app tiles — app cards and chart rows open on any click (not just the Open/Add button), with full keyboard support
v0.3.0 — deep visual parity & feature expansion
Canva-exact selection chrome — selection border and handles re-skinned to the measured purple #7630D7 with white circular anchors, 2px border and rotation snapping
Alignment guides recolored to the measured guide purple #9954FF at 2px
Context toolbar in the topbar — selecting an element swaps the topbar middle for a Canva-style toolbar (32px / r10 buttons): font dropdown with live previews + search + category pills, size stepper, colour menu, B/I/U/S/Uppercase, alignment, spacing, transparency, effects and position
Canva-style colour menu — spectrum + eyedropper + current colour, Brand Kit swatches, 4×7 default solids and gradient swatch rows
Text effects: 10 presets — Drop, Lift, Glow, Hollow, Outline, Background, Splice, Neon and Echo in a 3-column thumbnail grid
Position popover — 2×2 layer ordering (forward/backward/to front/to back), 6 align-to-page tiles and W/H/X/Y/Rotate numeric fields with ratio lock
Right-click context menus — element & page variants with keyboard shortcuts, layer ordering, group/lock/hide and delete (244px, 32px items, 13px)
Groups — Ctrl+G / Ctrl+Shift+G group & ungroup; children move and scale together
Marquee selection — drag on empty canvas to box-select; space+drag or middle-mouse to pan; Ctrl+A select-all
Zoom dropdown —
